results.title: Natural-Language Mediation Versus Numerical ...
results.content: Building on prior conceptual work proposing an advisory governance layer for AI systems, we designed a controlled experiment comparing a language-based mediator with a numerical baseline (Borda count) across 1024 synthetic stakeholder scenarios, each executed ten times (10,240 paired decisions). This paper investigates that gap through a controlled experiment comparing two decision mechanisms operating on identical preference–option scenarios: a conventional numerical aggregator (Borda count) and a language-based multi-agent system (MAS) powered by LLMs. By holding stakeholder configurations constant, we isolate how narrative reasoning alone influences agreement, fairness, and stability—dimensions central to governance design. Building on prior conceptual work proposing advisory layers for AI-assisted governance systems [9], this study empirically tests whether large language model (LLM) agents can perform the kind of narrative mediation assumed in such frameworks. **RQ1**—Reliability: To what extent can an LLM-based mediator, given only categorical stakeholder preferences expressed in natural language, reach decisions consistent with established aggregation baselines such as Borda count?
